summary: Bolivia's Migration Directorate (DIGEMIG) sorts passports into three groups: Group I countries do not require a visa, Group II countries require a consular visa or an entry permit issued by the Bolivian immigration office, and Group III countries require a consular visa. Bolivia's migration regulation (Supreme Decree 1923) says a tourist or visit visa is granted for 30 calendar days and that the stay for tourists is 90 calendar days at most per year. The UK government tells British nationals they can visit for up to 90 days without a visa, Australia's Smartraveller says Australians do not need a visa for tourism, and Hong Kong's government says HKSAR passport holders can apply for a tourist visa on arrival for a stay of 30 days.

vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Bolivia if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. Bolivia's Migration Directorate lists a yellow fever vaccination certificate among the requirements for a tourist stay permit if you will visit high-risk endemic areas.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bolivia travel advice: entry requirements (yellow fever)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Bolivia. The UK Foreign Office says you may not be able to access the public health system as it is already overstretched, that private clinics in all main cities work with international insurance, and that it is very important to have travel insurance and access to funds, as you will need to pay up front to receive treatment.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bolivia travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: No official Bolivian source we could read states an onward-ticket requirement. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask you to show a return or onward ticket, and Australia's Smartraveller says you may need to show proof of onward travel on entry.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Bolivia (entry and exit requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: No official Bolivian source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount. Canada's travel advice says customs officials may ask for proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Bolivia (entry and exit requirements)

declarations.name: Customs declaration
declarations.text: Bolivia's customs service says that before entering or leaving Bolivia you fill in Form 250 for new goods (on entry) and currency (on entry and exit) carried in your accompanied baggage. The form is available pre-printed or electronically.

source.name: Aduana Nacional de Bolivia — Declaración de equipaje y divisas (Form. 250)

currencyLimits.text: Bolivia's customs service says currency between USD 10,000 and USD 50,000 must be declared on entry, and between USD 10,000 and USD 20,000 on exit, and that larger amounts must be moved through financial institutions regulated by ASFI. It withholds 30% of undeclared currency, and 30% of the excess over USD 50,000 on entry or USD 20,000 on exit.

source.name: Aduana Nacional de Bolivia — Declaración de equipaje y divisas (Form. 250)

notes: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export any item that the Bolivian government considers a national treasure (patrimonio cultural) without formal written permission from the Ministry of Culture, including pre-Columbian artifacts, historical paintings, items of Spanish colonial architecture and history, native textiles, and flora, fauna and fossils.
Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to import coca leaves and related products into Canada.

Bolivia's customs service says travellers may bring in, as part of their allowance, used clothing and personal effects and new articles strictly for personal use, without commercial purpose, worth up to US$1,000, with limits of up to 3 litres of alcoholic drinks and 400 cigarettes; any goods exceeding the allowance must pay customs taxes.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit and debit cards are not widely accepted outside urban centres, recommends carrying small bank notes for daily transactions such as street food, taxis and tips, and says it is difficult to exchange Canadian dollars, so bring U.S. dollars if you need to exchange cash. The UK government says Bolivia is experiencing an economic crisis and dollar shortage.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to the Chapare region of Cochabamba Department, and says a State of Emergency gives police and armed forces powers to remove roadblocks. It says tourists, especially those travelling alone, are at risk of express kidnapping, that thieves can impersonate police officers, and that robberies from people taking taxis have increased in Santa Cruz, La Paz and Rurrenabaque; it advises ordering taxis by phone ('radio taxis').

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says you are at risk of high-altitude illnesses if you travel 2,500 metres above sea level or more, naming La Paz (3,640 m), Uyuni (3,656 m), Oruro (3,735 m) and Potosí (4,090 m), and that you are more at risk if you ascend quickly or exercise or drink alcohol before you get used to the altitude. It says high-altitude illnesses can be fatal.

Canada's travel advice says it is difficult to exchange Canadian dollars in Bolivia and to bring U.S. dollars if you need to exchange cash. Bolivia's Migration Directorate prices its tourist stay procedure in UFV (250 UFVs for up to 30 days).

The UK government's travel advice says protest groups often use road blockades as a form of protest, without warning, tells travellers not to attempt to cross blockades, and says recent blockades have led to fuel and fresh food shortages in some areas. Canada's advice says roadblocks are common throughout the country.
Bolivia's migration regulation (Supreme Decree 1923) says the stay for tourists is 90 calendar days at most per year.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bolivia?
faq.answer: Bolivia's Migration Directorate (DIGEMIG) sorts passports into three groups: Group I countries do not require a visa, Group II countries require a consular visa or an entry permit issued by the Bolivian immigration office, and Group III countries require a consular visa. The UK government tells British nationals they can visit for up to 90 days without a visa; Australia's Smartraveller says Australians do not need a visa for tourism; Canada's travel advice says a tourist visa is not required for stays up to 30 days; and Hong Kong's government says HKSAR passport holders can apply for a tourist visa on arrival for a stay of 30 days. Bolivia's migration regulation (Supreme Decree 1923) says the stay for tourists is 90 calendar days at most per year.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Bolivia?
faq.answer: Bolivia's migration regulation (Supreme Decree 1923) says the stay for tourists is 90 calendar days at most per year. The UK Foreign Office tells British travellers that border officials issue 30-day stamps but that they can stay 90 days without any new stamp; Australia's Smartraveller says the stay permitted on entry is 30 days and can be extended to 90. The Migration Directorate's procedure for a transitory stay for tourism or visit of up to 30 or 60 days costs 250 UFV for up to 30 days and asks for a tourist or visit consular visa.

faq.question: Can I really get a Bolivian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: No official Bolivian page we could read describes a visa on arrival. Hong Kong's Immigration Department says, citing Bolivia's embassy in China, that HKSAR passport holders can apply for the tourist visa upon arrival in Bolivia for a stay of 30 days. No official source we could read states the fee or processing time.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Bolivia?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Bolivia if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. Bolivia's Migration Directorate also lists one among the requirements for a tourist stay permit if you will visit high-risk endemic areas.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: Floods and landslides are common, particularly in mountainous areas during the rainy season (November to March), although weather can be unpredictable throughout the year. Roads can become impassable for days at a time.
Forest fires are common during the dry season (May to October) and affect some parts of Southern and Eastern Bolivia.
